Fixed. IPv6 literal brackets are no longer percent-encoded in link destinations, so `[visit](http://[2001:db8::1]/)` renders as `<a href="http://[2001:db8::1]/">`.

**Cause:** `normalizeLink` in `src/markdownit.ts` runs `mdurl.format()`, which re-adds the brackets around an IPv6 hostname. It then passes the whole string to `mdurl.encode()`, which percent-encodes `[` and `]` because they are not in its safe set.

**Fix:** In `src/markdownit.ts`, when the hostname contains `:`, `normalizeLink` now encodes the text before the `[host]` segment and after it, and keeps the bracketed host literal. Every other URL goes through the same `mdurl.encode(...)` call as before. The path, query and fragment are still encoded, so `a[b]` and `?c=[d]` still become `%5B`/`%5D`.

**Test:** I added "Should keep IPv6 literal brackets in link destinations" to the `Misc` block in `test/markdown-it/misc.test.mjs`. It checks the reported example and also a case with a port and bracketed path and query characters.

**Results:** `node --test "test/markdown-it/**/*.test.mjs"` passes, 301 of 301 tests, including the new one. I did not run the project's lint or type-check scripts.
